brief.Observed evidence: ANC participation shows a strong socioeconomic gradient across the pathway. Any ANC ranged from 53.9% in the poorest quintile to 95.0% in the richest. Among women reaching ANC4+, ANC8+ was 19.9% in the poorest versus 51.7% in the richest. The difference also remained among early initiators.
brief.Model evidence: Household wealth was the leading full-cohort XGBoost SHAP predictor and remained the highest-ranked shared predictor after early ANC timing was added.
brief.Programme-review cue: Review whether barriers affecting poorer women persist beyond initial ANC access and continue through repeated contacts.
brief.Contextual lenses: Travel time; maternal occupation; pregnancy intention
brief.Key caution: The analysis identifies an equity pattern but does not establish which financial, geographic or service mechanism causes it.

brief.Observed evidence: ANC entry and subsequent attainment decline as travel time increases. Any ANC was 86.5% at 0–30 minutes versus 54.7% at >120 minutes. Among early initiators, ANC8+ was 48.2% at 0–30 minutes versus 18.5% at >120 minutes.
brief.Model evidence: Travel time was among the strongest predictors in both the full-cohort and ANC-entry models and remained highly prominent after early ANC timing was introduced.
brief.Programme-review cue: Review where geographic and repeated-travel burdens interfere with both ANC entry and sustained attendance.
brief.Key caution: The empirical pattern does not determine which access or service-delivery response would be effective.

brief.Observed evidence: The stage at which ANC gaps become visible differs across regions. Somali shows a major entry deficit, while Central Ethiopia, Tigray, South Ethiopia and Sidama show different patterns of weaker timing or later continuation. Afar shows a particularly strong travel-related entry difference.
brief.Model evidence: Region was consistently among the leading predictors across algorithms and remained highly ranked after early ANC was added.
brief.Programme-review cue: Diagnose the pathway stage responsible for each regional pattern before considering a programme response.
brief.Contextual lenses: Travel time; religion; local service context
brief.Key caution: Region is a contextual marker containing many social, geographic and health-system influences. It is not itself a causal mechanism.

brief.Observed evidence: ANC8+ was 42.4% among early initiators compared with 11.1% among later initiators. However, 57.6% of early initiators still did not attain ANC8+, showing that timely initiation alone does not ensure completion of the recommended contact schedule.
brief.Model evidence: Early ANC ranked first in permutation importance across all three extended models and first in XGBoost SHAP. Frozen model-response contrasts were positive across algorithms, but paired performance confidence intervals for adding early ANC included zero.
brief.Programme-review cue: Review timely initiation and continuity after initiation as related but distinct programme problems.
brief.Contextual lenses: Household wealth; travel time; region; maternal occupation
brief.Key caution: Neither the observed difference nor the model-response contrast is a causal estimate of the effect of initiating ANC early.

matrix.Model evidence: Consistently prominent: full-cohort permutation ranks 2/2/1 and XGBoost SHAP rank 1; remains highly prominent after early ANC is added.
matrix.Observed pathway pattern: Large wealth differences appear at ANC entry, progression to ANC4+, early initiation, and ANC8+ attainment. Among early initiators, ANC8+ was 19.1% in the poorest quintile versus 62.4% in the richest.
matrix.Programme-review question: Which barriers affecting poorer women remain after they enter ANC and even when initiation is timely?
matrix.Additional evidence needed: Local information on direct and indirect costs, transport, service availability, appointment continuity, outreach and financial-access arrangements.

matrix.Model evidence: Full-cohort SHAP rank 2 and XGBoost permutation rank 3; remains among the leading predictors after early ANC is added.
matrix.Observed pathway pattern: Longer travel is associated with lower ANC entry, lower progression to ANC4+, and lower ANC8+ attainment. Even among early initiators, ANC8+ declined from 48.2% at 0–30 minutes to 18.5% at >120 minutes.
matrix.Programme-review question: Where does repeated travel burden interfere with timely entry and sustained ANC attendance?
matrix.Additional evidence needed: Facility catchment geography, service distribution, outreach coverage, transport availability, referral arrangements and local travel-cost information.

matrix.Model evidence: Highly consistent across algorithms: full-cohort permutation ranks 1/1/2 and SHAP rank 3; extended-model permutation ranks 2/2/2.
matrix.Observed pathway pattern: Regional patterns differ by pathway stage. Somali shows a large ANC-entry deficit; Central Ethiopia and Tigray show stronger entry but weaker later continuation; Afar shows lower entry but comparatively stronger continuation among women progressing through ANC.
matrix.Programme-review question: At which ANC stage does each regional gap emerge, and what local service or population context corresponds to that stage?
matrix.Additional evidence needed: Regional and woreda routine-service data, facility readiness, service organisation, workforce, outreach, access conditions and programme implementation information.

matrix.Model evidence: Ranked first by permutation importance in all three extended models and first by extended XGBoost SHAP. Incremental performance point estimates improved, but all paired confidence intervals included zero.
matrix.Observed pathway pattern: ANC8+ was 42.4% among early initiators versus 11.1% among later initiators. However, 57.6% of early initiators still did not reach ANC8+.
matrix.Programme-review question: How can programmes distinguish barriers to timely initiation from barriers to continuity after timely initiation?
matrix.Additional evidence needed: First-contact processes, pregnancy identification, scheduling, return-visit systems, appointment adherence and continuity-of-care information.

matrix.Model evidence: More prominent in the ANC-entry extended models: permutation ranks 5/3/5 and XGBoost SHAP rank 5.
matrix.Observed pathway pattern: Occupation groups show different pathway profiles rather than a simple ordered gradient. Professional/clerical women show high entry and early initiation, while differences among other groups change across later ANC stages.
matrix.Programme-review question: Do work conditions, time availability, livelihood patterns or service schedules contribute to different ANC attendance pathways?
matrix.Additional evidence needed: Local work schedules, seasonal livelihood patterns, clinic hours, waiting time, opportunity costs and qualitative evidence from women.

matrix.Model evidence: Consistently prominent in the full-cohort models with permutation ranks 3/3/4 and XGBoost SHAP rank 4; remains prominent in the extended ANC-entry model.
matrix.Observed pathway pattern: Religion-group differences occur at entry, timing and later attainment. For example, Protestant women had near-national ANC entry but lower early initiation and lower ANC8+ after ANC4+. Patterns differ from those observed among Muslim women.
matrix.Programme-review question: What geographic, social, community or service-context factors underlie these observed group differences?
matrix.Additional evidence needed: Region, residence and service-context information plus locally appropriate qualitative evidence. Religion itself should not be treated as the causal mechanism.

matrix.Model evidence: Prominent particularly in XGBoost/SHAP, but less consistent across algorithms than the leading predictors.
matrix.Observed pathway pattern: ANC entry was lower among women reporting the pregnancy was wanted no more, while progression to ANC4+ was lower among both 'wanted later' and 'wanted no more' groups than among women reporting 'wanted then'.
matrix.Programme-review question: Does reproductive context identify women who need additional support to remain engaged with ANC after entry?
matrix.Additional evidence needed: Family-planning and pregnancy-intention context, counselling pathways, social support and qualitative evidence. Retrospective intention reporting should be interpreted cautiously.

core.What Notebook 4 shows: Large differences are visible at ANC entry, progression to ANC4+, early initiation and ANC8+ attainment. The wealth gradient remains visible even among women who initiated ANC early.
core.Programme-review focus: Determine whether poorer women face barriers not only to entering ANC but also to sustaining repeated contacts after entry.
core.Options/issues to examine: Affordability of repeated attendance, indirect costs, transport burden, outreach coverage, service availability and continuity arrangements for economically disadvantaged women.
core.Guidance anchor: National ANC guidance emphasizes equity, demand, utilization and achievement of the recommended ANC contact schedule.
core.Local verification needed: Routine ANC data by socioeconomic proxy where available, transport and service-cost information, outreach coverage, qualitative evidence from women and facility-level continuity practices.
core.Boundary: Wealth is an equity signal. The analysis does not identify which financial or service mechanism causes the observed differences.

core.What Notebook 4 shows: Longer travel time is associated with lower ANC entry, later initiation and weaker progression toward ANC8+. Differences remain visible among women who initiated ANC early.
core.Programme-review focus: Identify where geographic access and repeated travel burden may interfere with both ANC entry and continued attendance.
core.Options/issues to examine: Catchment configuration, outreach arrangements, availability of nearer service points, transport conditions and other context-adapted ANC delivery arrangements.
core.Guidance anchor: WHO implementation guidance allows ANC delivery approaches to be adapted to context, including facility and community/outreach delivery.
core.Local verification needed: Facility and catchment maps, travel-time information, outreach coverage, transport availability, service readiness and local attendance patterns.
core.Boundary: Travel time identifies an access pattern but does not establish which service-delivery model would be effective.

core.What Notebook 4 shows: Regional differences arise at different ANC pathway stages. Some regions show particularly weak entry, while others show relatively strong entry but weaker later continuation.
core.Programme-review focus: Diagnose the ANC pathway stage at which each regional gap becomes most visible before selecting a programme response.
core.Options/issues to examine: Regional and woreda differences in service availability, workforce, facility readiness, outreach, access conditions, scheduling and programme implementation.
core.Guidance anchor: National and WHO guidance support context-sensitive implementation of ANC while maintaining the same overall standards for timely and continued care.
core.Local verification needed: Routine ANC indicators by region and woreda, facility readiness, workforce and service-organization data, outreach implementation information and local qualitative evidence.
core.Boundary: Region is a contextual diagnostic marker, not a causal mechanism or intervention target.

core.What Notebook 4 shows: ANC8+ attainment is substantially higher among early initiators, and early ANC is the most prominent predictor in the extended models. However, more than half of early initiators still do not reach ANC8+.
core.Programme-review focus: Separate the problem of timely initiation from the problem of continuity after timely initiation.
core.Options/issues to examine: Early pregnancy identification and first-contact pathways, followed by appointment scheduling, return-visit systems and continuity of care after the first ANC contact.
core.Guidance anchor: National and WHO ANC guidance recommend the first contact within the first trimester and a minimum of eight contacts.
core.Local verification needed: Gestational age at first contact, return-contact patterns, scheduling and appointment systems, missed-return information where available and facility-level continuity practices.
core.Boundary: The strong observed and model association does not establish a causal effect of early initiation, and its incremental predictive gain remains uncertain.

overlays.Observed Notebook 4 pattern: Occupation groups show different ANC pathway profiles rather than a simple socioeconomic gradient. Professional/clerical women had particularly high ANC entry and early initiation, while differences among other groups varied across later stages.
overlays.How to use in programme review: Use occupation to ask whether work schedules, livelihood demands, seasonality, clinic hours or opportunity costs help explain an identified access or continuity problem.
overlays.Evidence needed before interpretation: Clinic opening hours, waiting time, livelihood patterns, work flexibility and qualitative evidence from women.
overlays.Boundary: Occupation categories are not an ordered socioeconomic scale and should not be interpreted as causal effects.

overlays.Observed Notebook 4 pattern: Differences are visible across ANC entry, early initiation and later attainment. Protestant women had approximately national-level entry but lower early initiation and lower ANC8+ after ANC4+, whereas the pattern among Muslim women also included weaker entry.
overlays.How to use in programme review: Use the signal to investigate whether geography, community context, communication, service organization or other correlated conditions help explain an observed pathway difference.
overlays.Evidence needed before interpretation: Regional and residence distribution, service context, community engagement information and locally appropriate qualitative evidence.
overlays.Boundary: Religion is treated as a contextual marker, not as an intrinsic barrier, mechanism or programme target.

overlays.Observed Notebook 4 pattern: ANC entry was lower among women reporting that the pregnancy was wanted no more. Progression to ANC4+ was also lower among women reporting 'wanted later' or 'wanted no more' than among those reporting 'wanted then'.
overlays.How to use in programme review: Use reproductive context as a secondary lens when examining early engagement and continued ANC participation.
overlays.Evidence needed before interpretation: Family-planning context, counselling pathways, social support, pregnancy acceptance and qualitative evidence.
overlays.Boundary: This was a deliberately limited deep dive. Pregnancy intention is retrospectively reported and should be interpreted cautiously.

guidance.Guidance anchor: Minimum eight ANC contacts, with the first contact in the first trimester up to 12 weeks.
guidance.Relevant Notebook 4 signals: Early ANC initiation; ANC4+ to ANC8+ continuation
guidance.Programme relevance: Provides the national standard against which timing and continuity gaps can be reviewed.
guidance.Interpretation boundary: Notebook 4 measures observed attainment patterns, not compliance of individual facilities with the guideline.

guidance.Guidance anchor: ANC programme implementation should address equity, quality, standardization, demand and utilization.
guidance.Programme relevance: Supports examining whether ANC access and continuity differ across population and geographic contexts.
guidance.Interpretation boundary: Observed subgroup differences do not identify the specific health-system mechanism responsible.

guidance.Source: WHO Recommendations on Antenatal Care for a Positive Pregnancy Experience (2016)
guidance.Guidance anchor: ANC should provide a minimum of eight contacts and the first contact should occur within the first 12 weeks of gestation.
guidance.Programme relevance: Supports treating both timely initiation and sustained contact as distinct programme-review dimensions.
guidance.Interpretation boundary: WHO recommendations provide programme standards; Notebook 4 does not estimate the causal effect of meeting those standards.

guidance.Guidance anchor: Countries may adapt ANC delivery to context, including care through trained providers at facilities or through community outreach services.
guidance.Relevant Notebook 4 signals: Travel time; wealth; regional access patterns
guidance.Programme relevance: Provides an evidence-based basis for reviewing alternative service-delivery arrangements where repeated travel burden is substantial.
guidance.Interpretation boundary: Notebook 4 cannot determine which delivery model would be effective in a particular region or woreda.

guidance.Guidance anchor: Group ANC and community-based communication/support approaches require attention to context, women's preferences, trained facilitators, infrastructure and implementation resources.
guidance.Programme relevance: These approaches may be considered as review options where local evidence suggests access, communication or continuity barriers.
guidance.Interpretation boundary: Group ANC should not be presented as a proven solution from Notebook 4; WHO implementation guidance includes important context and research considerations.

guidance.Source: WHO community mobilization guidance for maternal and newborn health
guidance.Guidance anchor: Community participation and women's-group approaches can support maternal and newborn health, community support and use of skilled care.
guidance.Relevant Notebook 4 signals: Early initiation; religion/context; regional entry gaps
guidance.Programme relevance: Supports investigating community-level engagement where ANC entry or timely initiation is weak.
guidance.Interpretation boundary: Applicability should be assessed locally and should not be inferred directly from subgroup associations.

roles.Reason: Highly consistent model prominence and clear observed differences across entry, timing and later ANC attainment.
roles.Interpretation caution: Does not identify which financial, geographic or service mechanism produces the observed wealth differences.

roles.Reason: Strong model prominence and a clear observed gradient across ANC entry, early initiation and continuation.
roles.Interpretation caution: Travel time is a contextual access measure and does not by itself identify the service-delivery solution.

roles.Reason: Highly consistent model prominence and distinct regional pathway patterns across entry, timing and continuation.
roles.Interpretation caution: Region is not itself a mechanism or intervention target; it carries multiple geographic, social and health-system contexts.

roles.Reason: Strongest predictor in the ANC-entry extended models and strongly associated with observed ANC8+ attainment.
roles.Interpretation caution: Strong model prominence does not establish a causal effect, and incremental predictive improvement remains uncertain.

roles.Reason: Prominent in ANC-entry models and associated with differing patterns of entry, timing and later attainment.
roles.Interpretation caution: Occupation categories are not an ordered socioeconomic scale and may reflect work conditions, livelihood, wealth and other context.

roles.Reason: Consistently prominent across several models and associated with different observed ANC pathway patterns.
roles.Interpretation caution: Religion should not be interpreted as an intrinsic causal mechanism; regional, socioeconomic and service contexts may underlie the pattern.

roles.Reason: Relevant XGBoost/SHAP prominence and observed differences in ANC entry and progression to ANC4+, but less consistent across algorithms.
roles.Interpretation caution: Retrospective pregnancy-intention reporting requires cautious interpretation and the deep dive was intentionally limited.
